## Purpose

Renders the concierge chat lane that lives on every run screen — the message transcript, the
mode-switched composer (clarify/gate/building/complete/terminal), and the live agent-event
block strip (thinking, tool calls, file ops) inside each assistant turn. It is the first-class
chat surface for pre-run composing, mid-run steering, and post-run iteration described in the
run screen, and it is **presentational**: transport (SSE/WS, `sendMessage`, streaming state) is
owned by callers via hooks (`useRunChat`, `useChatAttachments`) and passed in as props.

## Shape

- [RunChatLane.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/RunChatLane.tsx) is the composition root (its own docstring calls it "the run-screen
  left-column composition root"). It renders [ChatPanel.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx) for the transcript and layers a
  single unified composer on top whose mode is driven purely by the generic `runState` prop
  (`idle | building | clarify | gate | complete | terminal` — never a workflow/agent name, the
  same `SC-001` discipline as the `workflow` module). It also renders the absorbed
  run-progress affordances (Stop, revise-as-chat, chain-suggestion chips, held Concierge
  proposal confirm/reject chips) and derives several live-only UI states from props:
  `replyPending` (Concierge round-trip spinner), the mid-reply "reading run data…" indicator
  (from `replyStreaming.lastChunkAt` gaps), and the collapsed `SettledSummaryStrip` (clarify
  count / pipeline mini / deliverable card).
- [ChatPanel.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx) owns the scrollable transcript: follow-the-bottom scroll behavior (via a
  `ResizeObserver` on the content wrapper, not just the messages array, so both chunk-clock and
  typewriter-frame growth are followed), the `role=log`/`aria-live` a11y contract, the
  empty-state greeting (suppressed when `hideComposer` — i.e. inside a run), and virtualization
  above `VIRTUALIZE_THRESHOLD` messages via [runtime/useMeasuredVirtualWindow.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/useMeasuredVirtualWindow.ts). Each row
  renders through [MessageBubble.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.tsx), which for assistant turns pulls per-message
  `AgentEvent[]` and reduces them with [runtime/buildBlocks.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/buildBlocks.ts) into a coalesced `ChatBlock[]`
  (text/thinking/tool/file_ops/usage), rendered via [runtime/tool-renderers.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/tool-renderers.tsx),
  [blocks/ThinkingBlock.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/blocks/ThinkingBlock.tsx), and [blocks/FileOpsSummary.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/blocks/FileOpsSummary.tsx). Narrator turns with a `cardKind`
  (`clarify | gate | pipeline | deliverable | spec_revision`) render as [ResultCard.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ResultCard.tsx) instead
  of prose, with a deep-link to the run's Preview/Steps/Files/Audit tabs via
  `onRequestOpenTab`.
- `runtime/` is the pure-function/parsing layer with no React: [buildBlocks.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/buildBlocks.ts) (event → block
  reducer, adapted from open-design's `AssistantMessage.buildBlocks`), [partial-json.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/partial-json.ts) and
  [streaming-json.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/streaming-json.ts) (extract a single named field from a still-streaming/open JSON fragment,
  e.g. a tool arg mid-stream), [blocks.types.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/blocks.types.ts) (the `AgentEvent` input union / `ChatBlock`
  render union contract), and [useMeasuredVirtualWindow.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/useMeasuredVirtualWindow.ts).
- Supporting leaf components: [ChatInput.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx) (the standalone composer used outside a run, when
  `RunChatLane` isn't mounted), [ChatAttachments.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ChatAttachments.tsx) (file/image intake shared by both
  composers), [LaneRunHeader.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/LaneRunHeader.tsx), [ChatTokenWidget.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ChatTokenWidget.tsx) (composed-context usage display, whose
  `composedContextUsage`/`COMPACT_THRESHOLD_PCT` are imported by `RunChatLane` so the
  compact-affordance threshold has one source of truth), [InlineClarifyActions.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/InlineClarifyActions.tsx) /
  [InlineGateActions.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/InlineGateActions.tsx) (quick-action answer surfaces), [ArtifactCard.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ArtifactCard.tsx)
  (exportable-deliverable card, wired to `lib/exporters/*`), [ProcessSteps.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ProcessSteps.tsx),
  [TypingIndicator.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/TypingIndicator.tsx), [ErrorMessage.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/chat/ErrorMessage.tsx).
- The SSE/WS live-state boundary sits entirely outside this module: `RunChatLane` and
  `ChatPanel` receive `messages`, `isStreaming`, `pipelineState`, `eventsByMessageId`, and
  `replyStreaming` as props from a caller-owned hook (`useRunChat`), and call back through
  typed props (`sendMessage`, `onApprove`, `onStop`, `onSuggestion`, ...) rather than touching
  a socket or fetch directly.

## Why this shape

The transport/presentation split (props and callbacks only, no fetch/EventSource in this
directory) is what keeps every component here testable against static fixtures and reusable
for both a live run and a settled/historical one — the same `ChatPanel` renders a completed
transcript from history exactly as it renders a streaming one.

Isolating the event-to-block reduction ([runtime/buildBlocks.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/buildBlocks.ts), [runtime/blocks.types.ts](../../frontend/src/components/chat/runtime/blocks.types.ts))
into pure functions is a direct consequence of that module being adapted from a third-party
reference (`open-design`, Apache-2.0, see `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`) as a clean-room
reimplementation — **keeping it React-free and side-effect-free makes it independently
testable and auditable** against the upstream behavioral spec without a build-time dependency.

The generic `RunLaneState`/`cardKind`/event `kind` discriminators (never a workflow or
agent-name literal) are the same `SC-001` invariant enforced in `components/workflow` — the
boundary protects against a crafted or unexpected workflow name ever selecting a privileged
renderer or composer mode.

Consequential actions (Concierge proposals, gate approve/redo) are deliberately held behind an
explicit confirm chip rather than auto-executed, and backend compaction is only ever
signaled/triggered from here, never performed here — **this module displays and requests, the
backend decides and acts.**
